title: Applications of Molecular Marker Technologies for Genetic Improvement of Sheep Production and Productivity
content: Sheep production contributes substantially to global food security and rural livelihoods by providing meat, milk, wool, skins, and other valuable products. Genetic improvement of economically important traits, including growth, reproduction, carcass quality, milk production, disease resistance, and environmental adaptation, is fundamental to increasing productivity and sustainability in sheep production systems. Conventional breeding methods based on phenotypic and pedigree information have achieved considerable genetic progress but remain constrained by low selection accuracy for complex, sex-limited, and late-expressed traits. Advances in molecular genetics have transformed sheep breeding by enabling the identification of genetic variants associated with desirable phenotypes and facilitating the implementation of marker-assisted and genomic selection strategies. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution and applications of molecular marker technologies in sheep breeding, from microsatellite markers to single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), genome-wide association studies (GWAS), genomic selection, and emerging next-generation sequencing (NGS) approaches. Particular emphasis is placed on the use of molecular markers for genetic diversity assessment, parentage verification, breed characterization, and the improvement of economically important traits, including reproduction, growth, meat quality, milk production, disease resistance, and environmental adaptation. Major candidate genes associated with prolificacy (BMPR1B/FecB, BMP15, and GDF9), muscle development (MSTN), meat quality (CAST and CAPN1), and adaptive performance are also discussed. Furthermore, the review highlights recent advances in genomic technologies, their integration into sheep breeding programs, and the opportunities and challenges associated with implementing genomic selection in both developed and developing countries. Overall, molecular marker technologies have substantially improved the precision of genetic evaluation and selection in sheep. Continued integration of high-throughput genomic tools, comprehensive phenotypic recording, and advanced bioinformatic approaches is expected to accelerate genetic gain and support the development of resilient, productive, and sustainable sheep production systems worldwide.
